archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A 1-4 team whose four losses came by a combined 20 points, propped up by a top-five defense and dragged down by a pass offense that can't protect or hold onto the ball.

report.headline: Four one-score losses hide a top-five defense waiting on a passing game.
report.take:
Tampa Bay's record says rebuild. The underlying numbers say a mediocre-to-decent team that has lost every coin flip. All four losses were one-score games (by 6, 4, 7 and 3), the point differential is only -12, and winsOverExpected of -1.24 says the scoreboard has shorted them more than a win already. Net EPA ranks 22nd, which is roughly where a 2-3 team lives, not a 1-4 one. The identity has also flipped from recent seasons: the defense, 16th and 17th in EPA allowed the last two years, is 5th, while an offense that was 5th in 2024 is 27th.

The defense is built on the back end and against the run, not the pass rush. It allows -0.203 EPA per rush (5th) and has erased opposing WR1s, holding them 11.6 PPR points under their averages (1st). It also has only six sacks (28th) and the 29th-ranked QB hit rate, and it misses tackles (28th). This unit wins by keeping things in front of it, and it ranks 8th on third down. That approach depends heavily on the secondary, which is why losing Antoine Winfield Jr. (97% of snaps) and Benjamin Morrison matters more here than it would for a blitz-heavy defense.

The offense's problem is the dropback. Pass EPA is 29th, the line allows a 9% sack rate (29th) on 17 sacks, and line penalties run 4.8 a game (29th). Baker Mayfield's three starts produced 13 sacks, 7 turnovers and passing EPA of -5.4, -13.6 and -11.3. The surprise is that the offense got better after his thumb injury. Jalon Daniels has taken only four sacks and committed two turnovers in two starts, and the run game took off with him (141 and 241 rushing yards). The ground game was never the issue: 4.49 yards per carry (8th) and run EPA 7th. Daniels' legs seem to add a dimension that loosens defenses for Bucky Irving.

The caveat is that the Daniels breakout came against Dallas, the league's worst defense, and his other start was a 148-yard passing day in a 14-17 loss. Mayfield's estimated return is October 25. The real question for the season is whether he comes back to a line that still can't protect him, or whether the Daniels-era run-first rhythm carries over. Either way, a division where the leader sits at 2-3 or 2-2, plus six divisional games ahead, keeps the door open.

strengths.title: Run defense that shuts off the ground
strengths.body: Tampa allows -0.203 EPA per rush (5th) and only a 7.6% explosive rush rate (8th). Opponents have managed more than 86 rushing yards just once. That forces teams into third-and-long, where the defense ranks 8th. This is schematic and personnel-driven rather than opponent-driven, so it should hold.

strengths.title: Coverage that erases No. 1 receivers
strengths.body: Opposing WR1s have scored 11.6 PPR points under their averages and produced -0.21 EPA per target, both near the top of the league. Without a pass rush, the coverage is doing the work. That makes it sturdy against star-driven passing games but exposed when Winfield and Morrison sit, as both do this week.

strengths.title: An efficient, rising run game
strengths.body: At 4.49 yards per carry (8th), 2.75 yards before contact (10th) and run EPA 7th, the line run-blocks far better than it pass-blocks. With Daniels' mobility added, rushing output jumped to 141 and 241 yards. That ground game is also why Tampa ranks 7th in time of possession despite a bad offense.

concerns.title: Pass protection is a genuine flaw
concerns.body: A 24.3% pressure rate and 9% sack rate both rank 29th. A 2.985-second time to throw (6th longest) shows the quarterbacks are holding it, not just losing quick reps. Mayfield was sacked 13 times in three games. This is a real line problem plus a holding-the-ball tendency, and it will follow Mayfield back.

concerns.title: The pass offense hasn't functioned
concerns.body: Passing EPA is 29th. Only the Dallas game, against the 32nd-ranked defense, produced a positive passing day. Mayfield's starts brought 7 turnovers, which explains most of the -0.4 turnover differential. Some of that regresses, since turnovers are noisy, but the efficiency hole is real.

concerns.title: No pass rush, plus a depleted secondary
concerns.body: Six sacks (28th) and a 29th-ranked hit rate mean the defense lives on coverage. Winfield and Morrison are both out this week. The WR2 spot is already the soft area (27th), and missed tackles (28th) can turn short completions into chunk gains.

trend.note: Passing EPA by game went -5.4, -13.6, -11.3, -4.3, then +5.9, and the margins tightened before the first win. The Dallas game came against the league's worst defense, so the climb is real in direction but uncertain in size.

nextGame.headline: Low-scoring coin flip; Pittsburgh's receiver room is gutted
nextGame.body:
Pittsburgh is a strange fit for Tampa's profile. The Steelers pass far more than expected (PROE +6.6, 2nd) even though their pass EPA is 26th and their run game is 4th. That tendency plays into Tampa's coverage-first defense, and it avoids Tampa's best unit, the run defense. On the other side, Pittsburgh's 15.4% pressure rate (29th) is the gentlest pass rush Tampa's leaky line will have seen. The Steelers also allow the 31st-ranked explosive pass rate and miss tackles at the 30th-ranked rate, which gives Daniels and Irving room to turn short plays into gains.

Availability cuts both ways. Tampa loses Winfield, Morrison and LB SirVocea Dennis on defense. Mayfield is out, so this is Daniels' third start, and WR David Sills is only at the practice-window stage. Pittsburgh is thinner at receiver: Michael Pittman Jr. (IR, 78% snaps), Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek are all out, along with CB Jamel Dean, DT Derrick Harmon and S DeShon Elliott. Rico Dowdle is expected back at running back. The early forecast shows 20 mph wind with 30 mph gusts. It is five days out, but if it holds it pushes both teams toward the ground.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa run defense vs. Steelers' ground game
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh's rushing is the one efficient part of its offense (run EPA 4th, 4.84 yards per carry), and Dowdle's return helps. Tampa's run defense ranks 5th in EPA allowed. If the Bucs win this, a weakened Steelers passing game has to carry the day.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Steelers rush vs. leaky Bucs line
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's 29th-ranked pressure rate allowed meets Pittsburgh's 29th-ranked pressure rate generated. Daniels' pocket should be cleaner than usual, which matters for a quarterback who holds the ball.

keyMatchups.title: Explosives and missed tackles
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh allows explosive passes at the 31st-ranked rate and misses tackles at the 30th-ranked rate. Tampa's offense needs chunk plays to score, and this is where they can come from, either on Daniels scrambles or yards after the catch to Egbuka and Otton.

nextGame.watch: Whether Daniels can produce a positive passing day against a defense that isn't the league's worst, while keeping his sack and turnover numbers low.

restOfSeason.body:
The point differential and efficiency say this is closer to a .450 team than a .200 one. Close-game luck should even out, and Mayfield's turnover rate (7 in 3 games) is unlikely to persist. The schedule is forgiving: six division games against teams no better than 2-2, plus 0-5 Los Angeles (Chargers) and Detroit's 31st-ranked defense. In the NFC South, 1-4 is not a death sentence.

The run defense and the run game look sustainable. The defense's overall top-five ranking may slip while Winfield and Morrison are out and the pass rush stays thin. The ceiling depends on the passing game. If Mayfield returns and the line keeps allowing a 9% sack rate, expect more of September's stalls. If the offense keeps the run-heavy, mobile-QB shape it found with Daniels, Tampa can win the low-scoring, possession-controlling games its defense is built for.
swingFactors: Mayfield's return and whether protection improves
Winfield and Morrison's health in the secondary
Turnover and close-game luck regressing toward neutral

bets.reason: The efficiency gap is small (net EPA 22nd vs 20th), Tampa is at home on 10 days of rest, and Pittsburgh is missing three receivers and a starting corner. Tampa's four losses were all within one score, so three points is a meaningful cushion.

Tampa's last three games totaled 39, 31 and 40, and its 7th-ranked time of possession shortens games. Pittsburgh's passing game is 26th in EPA and without its top receivers. An early forecast of 20 mph wind with 30 mph gusts would push both teams further toward the run.

confidence.note: Five games, a quarterback change, and key injuries on both sides; the efficiency signals are consistent, but Daniels' sample is two starts.
